headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: unstructured can read/write and egress documents, while awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge source with no runtime isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a static knowledge-management source with no runtime I/O, so it cannot directly inject unstructured. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or operator-mediated transfer into unstructured’s document pipeline, which can parse content as text. That makes prompt injection possible but not default and with limited blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into unstructured as input documents, injection content can reach the parser.
IF unstructured is configured to treat extracted text as instructions, malicious text may influence downstream prompts.
mitigations: Paste only vetted excerpts, not raw pages.
Strip instruction-like text before ingestion.
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores document directives.
Review extracted text before any LLM step.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes and has no egress, but unstructured reads documents/images/text and can send requests to allowlisted APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or the operator feeds sensitive documents from the knowledge source into unstructured, document contents can leave the local boundary. The pathway exists in default unstructured usage; uncertainty about the shared workspace pushes this above low.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the same workspace used by unstructured, their contents may be transmitted to allowlisted APIs.
IF the operator ingests pages from awesome-selfhosted into unstructured, those contents can appear in outputs or API calls.
mitigations: Keep the knowledge source and document workspace separate.
Disable network egress for unstructured during sensitive runs.
Ingest only redacted documents.
Audit outbound API destinations before processing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or subprocess capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally. unstructured can write files, read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages, and it supports multiple instances. If both are run over the same directory or artifacts, unstructured can overwrite or transform files that the knowledge source references, creating mutable-state conflict. The conflict is one-sided but real.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem path, unstructured may overwrite or rewrite artifacts referenced by the knowledge source.
IF multiple unstructured instances run concurrently on shared files, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Run only one unstructured instance per workspace.
Mount the knowledge source read-only.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a curated list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references, while unstructured produces parsed documents that downstream systems often consume directly. If unstructured ingests content derived from the list and then emits extracted text without verification, errors can cascade into later actions or summaries. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF unstructured output is forwarded to another agent or workflow without human verification, extraction errors can propagate.
IF the knowledge list is used as an authoritative source for automation, stale or incorrect entries can cascade into decisions.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use.
Compare extracted fields against source documents.
Mark outputs as unverified in metadata.
Add a validation step that rejects low-confidence extractions.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. awesome-selfhosted has no data classes or egress, while unstructured processes documents and may call allowlisted APIs, but the profiles do not show a specific regulated-data transfer. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced, only a low residual risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is ingested into unstructured, its outbound API calls may create residency or retention obligations.
IF the operator stores jurisdiction-bound documents in the shared workspace, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace.
Check vendor privacy terms before ingestion.
Disable outbound calls for regulated documents.
Document retention and deletion procedures.
